To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the vast majority of somatic missense cancer mutations have a high impact, and the majority of them affect protein function.

50-60 % of somatic missense cancer mutations are predicted to affect protein function, and that the majority of tumor suppressor mutations destabilize the protein structure, while the mutations in oncogeners operate in a more varied way.
the vast majority of somatic cancer mutations have a high impact, and that the impact of mutations in oncogenetic genes is more varied than the one for tumor suppressors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of methods to predict the functional impact of cancer somatic mutations.
the development and application of computational methods for analyzing somatic mutations in cancer genomes.
the development of computational methods for identifying the impact of cancer-related single-base substitutions and with the analysis of large data sets from cancer somatic genome projects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vast majority of somatic missense cancer mutations are predicted to affect the structure and function of their corresponding proteins.

a large fraction of all cancer somatic mutations are predicted to impact protein function and that the set of mutations that are predicted to have such an impact is a good starting point for the search for driver mutations.
the majority of mutations are likely to have functional effects and are therefore candidates for further investigation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a large number of cancer somatic mutations have a high impact in terms of structural stability and in vivo function.
the majority of cancer-related missenses are likely to affect protein structure and function in vivo.
a substantial fraction of all mutations have a high impact, with a much larger fraction of cancer mutations than human population SNPs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the vast majority of somatic mutations in cancers have a high impact, which is consistent with the view that these are the mutations driving tumorigenesis, and that these mutations have a much higher impact than nonsynonymous variants in the human population.
the majority of cancer somatic mutations are likely to be functionally relevant, and that the methods used for analyzing them can provide valuable insights into cancer mechanisms.
a significant fraction of cancer somatic mutations are likely to be functional and thus potentially driver mutations.
